points: Ramble freely. Don't tidy your thoughts first: sorting them and filing what's tangible is the advisor's job. One small habit helps a lot: name the repo or step when you know it.

Send every session question to the project chat; one advisor thread answers and rolls over to a fresh one at about 40 back-and-forths, a new batch, or a slip (see the hand-off guide). When a tangent belongs somewhere else, say 'park this'. It goes on the page as a note or a Later step, and the chat comes back to where it was.
Keep 'In progress' to two or three steps. Before starting another, finish or park one.
When it all feels like too much, open this page, read 'In progress' and 'Up next', and do only the first one.
For a decision you don't want to weigh, ask for the pick and a one-line reason, then take it unless it feels wrong.
Use fb: inside a Claude Code session for bursts aimed at that session. Use an advisor chat for anything about the plan or the system as a whole.
End every advisor chat with 'compare this chat against the page'.
Once a week, spend ten minutes on the page: flip statuses, look at anything off track, and take one thing to a new chat.
Say 'short version' when you've got the hang of something, and 'walk me through it' when it's new.

Threads in this project share one cap: 60 messages an hour to other threads and the coordinator (hit Oct 26 about 20:45 UTC, lifted 20:50). A refused send queues nothing, so the sender retries later. Standing threads batch routine notes so a hand-off is not held up. Unknown, unmeasured: whether Mac and PC sessions talking through SendMessage, or Remote Control reports back into a thread, count against it; no doc says.
summary: Tangents are fine. This is how to keep them from costing you.
title: How to use this project, given how you think
